record.file_problem: Not garbled or cut off. Several results are shown only in referenced figures, whose plotted values are not present in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Measures feature interpretability in a distilled transformer MLP using top-activating examples and a rubric, rather than the original neuron-visualization method.
record.gate_note: The post reports interpretability scores, a qualitative neuron example, and feature-type proportions across activation functions and sparsity settings. Encoder/decoder similarity and the toy convergence experiment do not measure polysemanticity; commenter reports are not results of the study.
record.test_reason: The post takes MLP neuron polysemanticity as its starting premise and reports how well its own method extracts interpretable features. That method distills one TinyStories MLP into a sparse 4x student. All rated units are student-model features, scored against an autoencoder; the original MLP's neurons are never scored. The claim that neuron simulators are 'no better than the original model's neurons' is asserted, not measured. The ReLU/GELU and L1 results describe the student dictionary's feature composition and reconstruction, not the prevalence of polysemantic neurons in a trained network.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Sparse distillation yields some interpretable sparse features, but neuron simulators do most of the reconstruction work and are no more interpretable than the original neurons. The method is worse than an SAE on reconstruction and monosemanticity and may miss multi-layer features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 4x-expanded student MLP trained to reproduce the original MLP's outputs with an L1 activation penalty; the main experiment uses ReLU. It does not reproduce the original neuron-visualization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported neuron-simulator share differs between ReLU and GELU at the same stated L1 coefficient. Reconstruction and feature activity also vary with the L1 penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: Student features that mimic original MLP neurons (decoder cosine >0.8) average 1.154/4 on the author's monosemanticity rubric, versus 2.833 for sparse features and 3.176 for SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary/distillation features that replicate original MLP neurons are rated far less monosemantic than sparse features (a method-evaluation result).

fits_no_version.finding: Using GELU instead of ReLU in the sparse student raises the share of neuron-simulator features from 29% to 70% at L1=2e-4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The activation function of a sparse distillation student affects how many of its features merely copy original neurons.

record.problems: Interpretability ratings are based on the author's rubric and inspection of the first 50 neurons. The study focuses on one model's second-layer MLP; several plotted results have no extractable numerical values in the text. Reconstruction error is reported, but downstream task performance after changing the feature composition is not.
record.rows_left_out: Left out the Figure 5 plotted proportions of dead neurons and neuron simulators across L1 settings because the supplied text gives no numerical values or sufficiently clear textual description of the simulator-share trend. Also left out encoder/decoder similarity and toy convergence results because they do not measure polysemanticity.

untested.parts: The original MLP neurons are never rated, and prevalence is not compared across layers or models.
Superposition is not tested as a cause.
Initialization, regularization and noise are not tested as causes.
The activation function and L1 are varied only in a distillation student. The share of polysemantic neurons in trained LMs and the task-performance cost are not measured.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not re-examined.
Activation range and scoring method are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its V2/V5 labels are not justified: every measurement concerns the study's own extraction method. The comment-thread results (Nabeshima's loss recovered) are not study results. The interpretability ratings come from a single author's rubric on 50 features each.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision neurons are studied.

Does not measure the prevalence of polysemantic neurons across language models, layers, or the original model's neurons as a population; the interpretability rubric is applied to the first 50 neurons of the distilled model and an autoencoder.
Does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than available neurons.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity when capacity is sufficient.
Tests ReLU versus GELU and varies L1 penalty in one distilled MLP; does not test modern convnets or establish downstream task performance after reducing polysemanticity.
Does not re-examine canonical polysemantic neurons to determine whether their mixed activations share a feature.
Uses top-activating examples and one rubric, but does not vary activation range or explanation-scoring method.
